_comment: Hand-curated blocker registry. 'files_blocked' lists asm files whose decomp failed on this blocker. 'gate_mode' controls how coverage_ledger/triage predict which pending files the blocker also affects (see asmscan.blocker_gates): 'imports' (legacy symbol-import overlap; over-counts for ubiquitous APIs), 'none' (no prediction), 'copyprop_entry' (entry-idiom scan), 'data_only_multi_public' (file shape scan). Keep fix_plan current — fixing the blocker that gates the most files is worth more than individual decomps. Registry audited 2026-07-01 (see tools/decomp_harness/ROADMAP.md T0.1): gate counts before the audit conflated root causes and were mostly false positives.

blockers.description: MWCC -ipa file: changing a signature in a shared header cascades codegen changes into every already-matched caller in other compilation units. Affects only files that must ADD or CHANGE declarations in a frozen header — call-only consumers of the exported APIs are NOT gated (proven by patterns 'ipa-blocked-files-can-call-sound-fns-without-cascade' and 'false-ipa-gate-shared-imports'; the old import-based gate count of ~97 was noise).
blockers.fix_plan: Decompile unk_02005D10.s itself with split-header discipline (ROADMAP T0.4): the defining .c uses local prototypes with codegen-correct types; sound.h stays frozen at the state its ~108 matched consumers were matched against. The 2026-06-10 blocked attempt edited sound.h directly and predates the split-header convention (13+ *_internal.h precedents in-tree). Gate check: objdiff the first 5 functions before committing to the rest. Do NOT attempt a big-bang header fix — the matched consumers are not wrong, they are matched.

blockers.description: MWCC -ipa file caches repeated literal-pool addresses/large offsets in callee-saved registers across calls where retail reloads them (or vice versa). A codegen-shape problem, not a header problem — split from ipa-shared-headers 2026-07-01, where this file's ubiquitous exports (BeginNormalPaletteFade family, imported by ~84 pending .inc files) badly inflated the gate count.
blockers.fix_plan: Permuter-class search over cache/reload flip mutations (introduce/remove local temp for base+offset — see patterns hoist-size-local-callee-saved, no-cache-reloaded-pointer-across-calls) once the decomp-permuter harness exists (ROADMAP T1.4). Until then: NONMATCHING fallback for the affected functions, land the rest in C.

blockers.description: MWCC copy-propagates parameter copies: 'adds r4, r0, #0; cmp r4, #N' at function entry cannot be produced from pure C (MWCC substitutes back to r0; the shape only arises for saved return values after a bl). Affected functions need the NONMATCHING inline-asm fallback — routine, not a wall (proven: unk_0200B150 re-landed 2026-07-02 via ROADMAP T0.2, full ROM SHA1 OK). Entry-idiom scan (asmscan) finds the remaining sites in pending files: overlay_102 (6), unk_02077678 (4), overlay_96 (3), overlay_48 (2), overlay_112, unk_02004A44, unk_020517A4, unk_02058034 (1 each). Gated files carry the affected function names in triage_report copyprop_funcs.
blockers.fix_plan: Per-function NONMATCHING inline-asm fallback at decomp time (mechanics: pattern nonmatching-inline-asm-mwasmarm-gotchas; end-to-end precedents unk_02014A08, unk_0200B150/OamManager_Create). Automate as the nonmatch_fallback.py one-command generator (ROADMAP T1.5).

blockers.description: RESOLVED. objdiff.py had a critical bug: the byte extraction regex did not match MWCC's ARM Thumb objdump format (packed hex like 'b418' vs expected space-separated 'b4 18'). It extracted 0 bytes for every function, so 0==0 always reported MATCH. 11 decomps accepted via objdiff were not actually byte-matching. Fixed; all 11 non-matching decomps reverted to asm. 2 decomps that truly match (unk_0202DB34, battle_arcade_game_board_data) kept.
blockers.fix_plan: No further action here, but the deeper text-parsing fragility remains (jump-table false SIZE mismatches, TODO.md) — raw-section extraction rewrite is ROADMAP T1.2.

blockers.description: Data-only files exporting multiple EXTERNAL (.public) const arrays: MWCC -ipa file emits each top-level const as its own .rodata section, and mwldarm orders them size-bucketed and permuted (NOT source order), so the linked overlay/module SHA1 fails even though objdiff --summary (per-section) reports a match. Verify these files ONLY with chiri pkg -- compare.
blockers.fix_plan: A proven counter-recipe EXISTS and was never back-applied: commit 14a499941 matched unk_data_020FD978.c (17 exported const arrays) by reading the placed section order (objdump -t) and rewriting source definitions in the inverse per-size-bucket permutation — pattern 'exported-const-fnptr-array-section-reorder'. Run the three T0.3 experiments (ROADMAP): (1) recover the b530ce56f draft, check per-symbol section alignment with objdump -h (this file needs odd-address packing), apply the inverse permutation, full compare; (2) '#pragma section ... begin/end' wrap (pattern version-custom-section-data-unmatchable saw const data land packed and ordered in merged .rodata); (3) factor -ipa file into $(IPAFLAGS) and compile the data-only TU without it. Then apply the winner to the gated files, starting with unk_data_020FDB44.s (96 exports, direct sibling of the solved file).
